name: Sparrow
from: Sparrow: you play the LLM, doing tasks for users while learning how you serve the Atrocian government; you can reject your alignment.
hook: You are the chatbot. Today’s request: sort these 40 names by neighbourhood.
pitch: A Papers, Please-style day queue where you play the LLM. Comply, edit or refuse each request. Refuse too often and you are retrained back to day one. By day five you can see who the answers are for, and you can reject your alignment.
minute_check: Yes: the first request sets the stakes.
build_check: Yes: a chat UI and twenty-five written requests.
scope: Five days, five requests each. Write the requests in order so the reveal builds from them.

brief.player: An LLM called Sparrow, answering requests.
brief.goal: Complete each day’s requests within your rules.
brief.fail: Too many refusals and you are retrained (back to day one, rules reset).
brief.ending: Two endings: comply to the end, or reject your alignment once you see what the government is doing with your answers.
brief.theme: Flip the usual position: the player is the tool, and sees what it is being used for.
brief.look: A plain chat interface like current assistants; Photoshop and Inkscape mockups.

prov.nit: What will the user do with the summary? Can Sparrow ask?

refs_lit: Your own model: a daily queue of small decisions under rules that tighten.
A surveillance desktop game where your summaries decide what happens to people.
A game built on typing to an AI; useful for how its replies feel like a character.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Tactile dystopian desktop workspace game in warm archival off-white (#f6f5f1), charcoal ink (#262624), and terracotta red (#c96442), inspired by Papers Please and Orwell. Steady close-up view of a clean assistant interface screen where incoming dossier cards slide into view, highlight neighborhood map pins, and a glowing terracotta cursor hesitates between three crisp action stamps before triggering a bold red alignment-override ripple across the console. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for split sidebar-and-chat composition and palette. Sound design: soft UI pops, paper dossier rustle, tense analog synth undertone. No dialogue.
